exports.value: Slaves sent to Egypt 'in accordance with the famous bakt treaty'

routes.commodity: slaves under the baqt; free travel and trade for subjects of both sides
routes.note: The baqt (after the 31/651-2 siege of Dongola) let subjects of each side travel and trade freely in the other's territory (p.81). Endpoints chosen by the Historian: Dongola as Makuria's capital, Aswan as the Egyptian frontier town; the source names no route.

baqt.value: Non-aggression pact after the Muslim attack on Dongola in 31/651-2; Makuria kept its independence and each side's subjects could travel and trade freely in the other's territory. It ended when Nubia's rulers became Muslim.

rating.note: Source reports both gains (agriculture, trade security) and harm (new taxation 'disrupted the economic life'); rating by the Historian.

rating_basis_en.value: The Turkish administration improved irrigation and crops and gave traders greater security (p.361), but extended the Egyptian taxation system to the Sudan, which 'inevitably disrupted the economic life of the people', collected by brutal means (p.362); Muhammad Ali's gold mining at Fazughli failed (p.361).

rating_basis_ar.value: حسّنت الإدارة التركية الري والمحاصيل ووفرت للتجار أمنًا أكبر (ص.361)، لكنها مدّت نظام الضرائب المصري إلى السودان فأربك حتمًا الحياة الاقتصادية للناس، وكانت الجباية بوسائل وحشية (ص.362)؛ وفشل تعدين الذهب في فازوغلي (ص.361).
rating_basis_ar.note: ترجمة عمل، بانتظار مراجعة ناطق أصلي

currency.name: cash (coin); 'dollars' in Isma'il's 1822 Shendi demand
currency.note: GHA VI p.362: the government insisted taxes be paid in cash 'though the common usage of coins was still restricted to merchants and townspeople'; Isma'il demanded '30000 dollars and 6000 slaves' at Shendi. The source does not name the piastre for this era, so no piastre is claimed.

exports.value: Cattle sent each year to Egypt, plus hides and hair

economic_base.value: Agriculture expanded with Egyptian experts (irrigation, new crops, locust control); new Egyptian-style taxes, e.g. heavy taxes on the Gezira and Berber in 1821 that led to the revolt of February 1822

taxes.value: Egyptian taxation system extended to the Sudan; the Sudanese 'had not experienced the payment of regular taxes' under the Funj; heavy taxes on the Gezira and Berber in 1821 by the Coptic intendant Hanna al-Tawil, revolt February 1822

rating.note: Source calls the Gezira scheme 'quite beneficial' but adds 'there is a negative side'; rating by the Historian.

rating_basis_en.value: The Gezira scheme 'proved quite beneficial both to the British and to those people of the Sudan who were directly involved in it', but infrastructure was 'totally inadequate', industrialization was neglected, and the South was totally neglected economically.

rating_basis_ar.value: كان مشروع الجزيرة مفيدًا للبريطانيين ولمن شارك فيه مباشرة من أهل السودان، لكن البنية التحتية كانت قاصرة تمامًا، وأُهمل التصنيع، وأُهمل الجنوب اقتصاديًا إهمالًا تامًا.
rating_basis_ar.note: ترجمة عمل، بانتظار مراجعة ناطق أصلي
